title: An online shop is not just a website
source: Written from general knowledge of online selling. No measured figures; labels on screen are not statistics.

lines.text: If I told you an online shop is not just a website, would you believe me?
Let me draw it for you, one branch at a time.
We will walk through eight branches, and every one connects back to your shop.
First branch: the website, the storefront of your shop.
Customers browse the home page, categories, products and search, then add to cart and pay.
Clear photos, full descriptions and honest prices make them feel safe.
But this is only the part customers can see.
Second branch: sales channels.
Customers are not in one place: they scroll social media, open marketplaces, or message you directly.
Some actively search, others stumble on a product and love it.
A shop that shows up in the right place is easier to find.
Third branch: bringing customers in.
A beautiful shop nobody knows about is like a store in an empty alley.
So you need ads, search, email and good content.
Paid ads give fast results, while content lasts longer but takes time.
Every dollar you spend must be measurable.
Fourth branch: products and stock.
Selling out loses customers, and too much stock freezes your cash.
So know how many of each product are left, and how fast it sells.
Slow items? Discount them or bundle them into a combo.
Fifth branch: payment and delivery.
Once the customer pays, the order must be packed and delivered on time.
Shipping fees and delivery time also decide whether they complete the order.
Delivered is not the end: there are returns and refunds.
Sixth branch: customer care.
A first-time buyer who is treated well comes back for a second, a third time.
That is a loop: buy, use, review, buy again.
A thank-you, a coupon for next time, or a friendly message helps them remember you.
Keeping old customers is usually lighter than finding new ones.
Seventh branch: data.
Every order and every visit leaves a number behind.
From them you see which product sells, where customers come from, and whether the shop is making or losing money.
Do not watch every number: pick a few key ones and check them daily.
Eighth branch: automation.
Repeating work, like order confirmations, payment reminders and daily reports, can be handed to a machine.
Machines never tire or forget, but you still set the rules.
People keep the part that needs thinking.
Let's look at the whole map.
Website, channels, ads, products, delivery, care, data and automation: all running together.
The website is only the leaf you see most.
Behind it is a whole operating system.
Understand the map, and you will know what to do next, and which branch is weak.
